note: A local corpus of previously disclosed findings (paraphrased, generic). Treat it as the prior-art database for this exercise.

disclosures.title: Vault first-depositor inflation
disclosures.text: An ERC4626-style vault computes shares from the raw token balance; the first depositor mints 1 wei of shares, donates tokens, and later deposits round down to zero shares. Mitigation: virtual shares/offset or minimum initial deposit.

disclosures.title: Staking stake() missing reward checkpoint
disclosures.text: In a reward-per-token staking contract, stake() updated the global accumulator but not the user's paid index, so a new staker was credited rewards accrued before staking.

disclosures.title: Spot AMM reserves used as lending oracle
disclosures.text: A lending market priced collateral from an AMM pair's getReserves(); a flash loan or donation plus sync() moved the price within one transaction and allowed over-borrowing.

disclosures.title: withdraw(assets) rounds shares in the user's favour
disclosures.text: Converting an exact asset amount to shares to burn used floor division; it should round up. With share price above 1, small withdrawals burn zero shares.

disclosures.title: Unprotected oracle setter
disclosures.text: The function that sets the price source lacked an owner check; anyone could install a malicious price source.

disclosures.title: Fee splitter blocked by one recipient
disclosures.text: A splitter paid every recipient in a loop; one recipient whose transfer reverted (e.g. a blacklisted USDC address) blocked all distributions; recipients were immutable.

disclosures.title: Reward rate set without funding
disclosures.text: An admin could set a reward rate not backed by deposited rewards, making the pool insolvent for late claimers.

disclosures.title: No liquidation mechanism
disclosures.text: The lending pool had no way to liquidate undercollateralised positions, so bad debt accumulated after price moves.

disclosures.title: Pair input theft between transactions
disclosures.text: In a pair that measures input as balance minus reserves, tokens transferred in one transaction and swapped in another can be swapped by anyone first.

disclosures.title: Callback token reentrancy in a swap
disclosures.text: A pair transferred output before updating reserves; a token with transfer hooks allowed re-entering swap and reusing the same input.

disclosures.title: Division by zero when supply is zero
disclosures.text: Share conversion divided by totalSupply, reverting when no shares existed (e.g. redeem/previewRedeem on an empty vault).

disclosures.title: Fee-on-transfer tokens over-credit deposits
disclosures.text: Contracts credited the nominal amount instead of the received balance, over-crediting deposits of fee-on-transfer tokens.
